subject: history
title: The Great Terror 1936-38
welcome_lead: Show trials, mass operations and the destruction of the Old Bolsheviks.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Stalin's purges and the gulag system 1936-38.
final_note: You have entered the bloodlands at their darkest.

concepts.def: Murder of Leningrad party boss Sergei Kirov on 1 December 1934, pretext for purges.
Public trials in 1936, 1937 and 1938 of Old Bolsheviks including Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin.
Mass operations under NKVD chief Nikolai Yezhov 1937-38; from Order 00447 of July 1937.
NKVD order of 30 July 1937 setting regional execution and camp quotas, targeting 'former kulaks' and criminals.
1937-38 elimination of three of five marshals and around 30,000 officers, weakening the military before 1941.
Soviet labour camp system named in Solzhenitsyn's 1973 work; population peaked at about 2.5 million in early 1950s.

walkthroughs.body_html: Kirov's death gave Stalin grounds to expand repression. The first show trial in August 1936 condemned Zinoviev and Kamenev. Yezhov replaced Yagoda as NKVD chief in September 1936. Order 00447 of 30 July 1937 launched the kulak operation with regional quotas; ethnic operations targeted Poles, Germans, Latvians and others. About 1.5 million were arrested and 750,000 executed.

walkthroughs.h2: Old Bolsheviks and the Red Army
walkthroughs.body_html: The Pyatakov-Radek trial in January 1937 and Bukharin's March 1938 trial eliminated remaining Old Bolsheviks. Tukhachevsky and seven generals were secretly tried and shot in June 1937, beginning the army purge. Three of five marshals, 14 of 16 army commanders and about 35,000 officers were dismissed or killed, contributing to Red Army weakness in 1941.

Robert Conquest's Great Terror (1968) portrayed Stalin as omnipotent puppet-master. Revisionists like J. Arch Getty and Sheila Fitzpatrick emphasised local dynamics, denunciations and regional officials. Oleg Khlevniuk's archival research after 1991 confirmed Stalin's central role in setting quotas and approving execution lists. Yezhov was removed in November 1938 and shot in 1940 as scapegoat.
